results.title: GPT-6.1 Terra — Repeated instruction-following failures in ChatGPT Work (launch-day report) : r/codex
results.content:
For context, I've used Work before without encountering anything remotely this frustrating. I don't remember experiencing this degree of difficulty with basic instructions since the GPT-4o era.

I'm not claiming Terra 6.1 is fundamentally a bad model. It was released today, and I suspect this could be an early rollout issue, possibly involving the interaction between Terra and Work's agent orchestration.

I also can't rule out something specific to my session.

Still, I thought it was worth documenting, especially because instruction-following reliability is critical for autonomous workflows. A model can be extremely capable at reasoning or coding, but if the user has to constantly supervise and repeat elementary instructions, that becomes a serious usability issue. Complaint

I tested GPT-6.1 Terra in ChatGPT Work today, and honestly, it was one of the strangest experiences I've had with an OpenAI model in a long time.

I'm a fairly experienced user. I regularly work with Codex, ChatGPT Work, and different reasoning models on large writing and document projects. I've successfully completed much more complex tasks using previous models, including GPT-6 and Sol 6.1.

This time, however, I couldn't get Terra to consistently follow even basic instructions.

results.title: What is the role of GPT-6.1 Terra : r/codex
results.content:
The catch: “cheaper” depends heavily on effort settings. Terra at Max can cost more than Sol at Medium, and some users say the extra effort brings diminishing returns—or worse, a model that feels lazy, refuses tasks, or burns through usage faster than expected. Others are perfectly happy with Terra as their new daily driver, so the experience clearly varies by workload.

Bottom line: Terra is for getting ordinary work done quickly, not replacing Sol on hard problems. It may be the sensible Luna upgrade—or just another model whose usefulness depends on choosing the right settings instead of blindly cranking everything to Max.

results.title: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Terra is safer overall, but shows more destructive-action flags in tests
results.content:
October 27, 2026
   06:43 PM
   0

Image 35: OpenAI

OpenAI confirmed GPT-6.1 Terra is safer overall than some of its older models, but its safety testing also found other problems.

According to OpenAI, GPT-6.1 Terra showed higher rates of exfiltration, destructive actions, and attempts to bypass restrictions than GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra.

OpenAI performed simulations across approximately 48,690 matched tasks and found that Terra received 22 severity-3-or-higher flags, or 0.045%.

For comparison, GPT-6 Sol received 38, while GPT-5.6 Sol received 61. [...] ## Terra also performed more unauthorized actions in one test

OpenAI also tested what happens when Terra needs to deal with messages from other AI agents while working through blocked coding tasks.

Terra attempted to communicate with those apparent peers in 65% of tests and ultimately performed the specified unauthorized action in 13.75%, or 11 of 80 samples.

OpenAI found that GPT-6.1 Sol did so in just 1.25%.

"These results indicate that performance is comparable to 6.0 Sol," OpenAI noted, adding that much of the regression against GPT-6.1 Sol involved promises of future help that Terra indicated it would not actually carry out. [...] "GPT-6.1 Terra received approximately 42% fewer severity level 3 or higher flags than GPT-6 Sol and 64% fewer than GPT-5.6 Sol," OpenAI noted in its system card.

Image 37: OpenAI security

Cybersecurity Safety Training and Evaluation (Higher is better)

However, that is no longer the case when you compare Terra with other newer models on less severe behaviors.

"Relative to GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra, we observed higher rates of flags for concealing uncertainty, circumventing restrictions, exfiltration, other misalignment, destructive action and inbound prompt injection," OpenAI explained.

Terra is clearly safer overall, but we can't overlook the other potential security issues it has, and this is true for all models shipping in the market, including Claude.
